1  MFA No. 4649 of 2021  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 11.02.2021 PASSED IN MVC NO.905/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES, AS A PRESIDING OFFICER, MOTOR ACCIDENTS CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, MYSURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 11.02.2021 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mysuru (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.905/2017.
This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under; That on 01.03.2017 at about 5.45 p.m., the claimant was traveling in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 11-W-3819 as a pillion rider along with one N.Manjunath, NC: 2024:KHC:6383 when they reached near ring road junction, Nanjangud road,
Mysuru city, at that time, the driver of a car bearing registration No.KA-09-C-0395 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the claimant in which she is a pillion rider.
Due to the said impact, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, she was shifted to J.S.S.Hospital, Mysuru, wherein, she has taken treatment as an inpatient and spent huge amount towards medical expenditure.
3.1 It is stated that the claimant was hale and healthy prior to the occurrence of accident.
She was working as a tailor and earning an income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the occurrence of accident and injuries suffered, the claimant is unable to do her work normally as she was doing prior to the occurrence of accident.
Hence, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
3.2 On service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed ex parte.

Respondent No.2- Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed NC: 2024:KHC:6383 statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

Nagarathnamma vs Kumar on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183222440/
2 3.4
In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined herself as PW.2 and the Doctor as PW.4 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P29.

On the other hand,
respondent No.2 examined a witness as RW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 and R2.
3.5

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.4,43,500/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization and also held respondent Nos.1 and 2 to be jointly and severally liable to NC: 2024:KHC:6383 pay the compensation to the claimant and respondent No.2 being the insurer was directed to pay the compensation within 30 days from the date of the award.
3.6
Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court challenging the impugned judgment and award.

4. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meagre compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company contends that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.
Hence, he seeks dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for appellant-claimant and learned counsel for Insurance Company,
perused the NC: 2024:KHC:6383 impugned judgment and award, the documents produced at Exs.P1 to P29, the Police records and medical records, out of which the Police records clearly depict the filing of FIR and laying of charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and same has not been challenged or controverted.
Therefore, the tribunal rightly attributed the negligence against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The medical records, which clearly depicts the injury sustained by the claimant in the occurrence of accident.
7. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income, it is stated that age of the claimant was 48 years as on the date of occurrence of accident.
The tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '13', which does not call for interference.
8. The tribunal assessed the income of Rs.7,000/- per month, in view of there being no proof of income.

Though the claimant has stated that she was working as a tailor and earning more than Rs.15,000/-, no materials are produced before the Court to substantiate the same and it NC:
2024:KHC:6383 is self serving statement of the claimant.
It is vehemently contended by the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the Insurance Company has not specifically denied the averments to the effect that the claimant is doing tailoring work.

However, when a person approaches the Court and pleads a particular fact then the burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the Court to believe in its existence, unless it is provided by any law that the proof of that fact shall lie on any other person, which is contemplated under Section 103 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

sentences.text:
Though I agree with the learned counsel for appellant-claimant as there is no specific denial,
nevertheless it becomes the duty of the claimant to prove the fact what he pleads and wishes the Court to believe in the present facts of case.

No such material having been produced, the notional income chart of the Legal Services Authority prescribes the income of Rs.11,000/- for the NC:
2024:KHC:6383 accident year 2017.
Accordingly, income is taken as Rs.11,000/-.
10. PW.4-Doctor stated in his evidence with regard to the injuries sustained by the claimant and magnitude of the same and has opined the disability to the extent of 47% to the right lower limb.
However, he has not stated the disability to the whole body.

The tribunal, on appreciation of evidence on record, arrived at disability to the whole body at 16% by dividing disability of 47%
assessed by PW.4-Doctor from 1/3rd.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to the compensation of Rs.2,74,560/- (Rs.11,000/- x 12 x 13 x 16%) towards loss of future income as against Rs.1,75,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
11. The tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards pain and suffering.
I am in agreement with the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the same is on the lower side.
Considering the injuries suffered by the claimant, this NC: 2024:KHC:6383 Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.
12. The tribunal awarded Rs.14,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
In view of this Court enhancing the income from Rs.7,000/- to Rs.11,000/-, the claimant would require atleast four months period to recuperate and to get back to her normal day to day activities.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.44,000/- (Rs.11,000/- x 4) under this head.
13. The tribunal awarded Rs.11,500/- towards attendant charges, extra diet, nourishment and conveyance, whereas, the claimant was inpatient for 23 days.
I deem it appropriate to award Rs.25,000/- under this head.
14. The tribunal awarded Rs.5,000/- towards loss of amenities, which is on the lower side.
Considering the magnitude of the injuries and claimant was inpatient for - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:6383 23 days, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. Towards medical expenses, Rs.2,08,000/- is awarded by the tribunal on the basis of actual bills produced by the claimant, which also does not call for interference and the same is retained.
16. The tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.
PW.4-Doctor has opined that Rs.30,000/- to Rs.40,000/- is required for future medical expenses.
I deem it appropriate to award Rs.25,000/- under this head.
